margin_readings.object: Token-DiFR (and Activation-DiFR) checks whether a provider's inference follows a claimed specification. It compares the provider's sampled tokens with a trusted reference implementation of the same weights, run under a shared seed, to catch 4-bit or FP8 quantization, a wrong seed or temperature, and sampling bugs. Its null distribution comes from honest runs of the same checkpoint on different GPUs, parallelism setups and inference engines.
margin_readings.reason: B14 compares a model with a differently served copy of itself on a fixed prompt set, using a logit-based score, and grades that against a null built from honest runs of the same checkpoint on other hardware. It reports only detector AUC at 1% FPR, with no confidence interval or p-value on the compared quantity, and publishes no digest of its item set.
margin_readings.hardest_element_why: The paper states an H0 and fixes the false-positive rate at 1%, which looks like a stated alpha, but what it actually reports is classifier AUC at that FPR against an empirically set threshold, not a test result on the compared quantity at a stated level.

margin_readings.object: An LLM served under some configuration is checked against a trusted reference implementation of the same weights. The verifier teacher-forces the provider's claimed tokens and scores seed-synchronised post-Gumbel logit margins (Token-DiFR) or projected activations (Activation-DiFR). Deviations tested include 4-bit and FP8 quantization, FP8 KV cache, wrong seed or temperature, and sampling bugs, plus five public Llama 3.1 8B APIs. Verdicts are graded against a pooled honest null of the same weights run on different GPUs, parallelism and engines.
margin_readings.reason: The paper checks served outputs against a reference copy of the same weights (quantized, misconfigured, or third-party API) on a fixed prompt set, scoring with teacher-forced logits. Its null distribution comes from the same weights on different hardware and engines, and that null calibrates the detector. It gives no confidence interval and no test at a stated level on the compared quantity, only empirically set thresholds and AUC at 1% FPR. It publishes no digest of the prompts.
margin_readings.hardest_element_why: The paper states an H0/H1 hypothesis test (H0: only benign noise) and reports AUC at 1% FPR, which reads almost like a stated alpha; but the test is only described informally, its threshold is set empirically, and the reported number measures detector performance, not a test result or interval for a given comparison, so the definition is not met to its letter.

margin_readings.object: Logprob tracking (LT): an LLM API or local model is compared with itself at another time, or with small TinyChange variants of the same weights (fine-tuning, pruning, noise). The compared quantity is a permutation-test statistic on the mean top-k first-token logprobs for one fixed prompt. It is graded in vitro by ROC AUC against 1,000 original/original tests, and applied to 189 real endpoints hourly with a running-variance threshold.
margin_readings.reason: The paper runs a same-model comparison over time and across variants, on a fixed prompt, using logprobs. Null distributions come from 1,000 original/original tests on identical weights, and the ROC AUC is built on them. Overall and per-difficulty AUCs carry bootstrap 95% CIs. No digest of the item set is published.
margin_readings.hardest_element_why: The permutation test gives no numeric alpha and reports no p-values, so E4 rests on the 95% bootstrap CIs on the original-vs-variant AUC, and whether that AUC counts as the compared quantity is a matter of reading.

margin_readings.object: Logprob tracking: the method sends one fixed short prompt to a served LLM and runs a permutation test on the first-token top-k logprobs. It is used in two setups. The first compares an original local model with its TinyChange variants (fine-tuned, pruned, noised) and grades detection against 1,000 tests of the original model against itself. The second compares the same real-world API endpoint with itself hour by hour over months.
margin_readings.reason: The paper compares a served model with itself: the same API endpoint over time, and an original model against pruned, noised or fine-tuned variants. Both sides get the same fixed prompt, and the test statistic is built from first-token logprobs. In the TinyChange evaluation, detection is graded against a null distribution from original/original tests on identical weights. There is no interval on the compared quantity: alpha is never given a number, no p-values are reported, and the real-world flag is a 12-standard-deviation threshold with no stated level. The 95% bootstrap intervals are on ROC AUC pooled across models, which measures the detector, not the logprob distance. The prompt and code are public, but no digest is given.
margin_readings.hardest_element_why: The paper defines a permutation-test p-value with a 'no difference' null and reports 95% bootstrap intervals on ROC AUC. I coded E4 false because alpha is never given a number, no p-value is reported, and the intervals are on pooled detection performance rather than on the logprob distance between the two sides.

margin_readings.object: Logprob tracking: a permutation two-sample test on first-token top-k logprobs for a fixed one-token prompt, used to detect whether an LLM API or local model has changed. It compares the model with its own earlier self (189 real endpoints tracked hourly) and with fine-tuned, pruned or noised variants of the same weights (TinyChange), scored by ROC AUC against original/original null runs.
margin_readings.reason: The paper runs a self-comparison on a fixed prompt using API logprobs, and grades TinyChange detection with a null distribution from original/original tests on identical weights (E1, E2, E3, E5). Its permutation test sets alpha only as "the chosen significance level" with no value, and no p-value is reported. Its 95% CIs are on the detector's AUC pooled across models and variants, not on the compared quantity. Real-world flags use a 12-SD threshold with no stated level. So E4 is false, and no digest is published for the item set, so E6 is false.
margin_readings.hardest_element_why: The paper defines a hypothesis test with null "identical" and reports 95% bootstrap CIs, but alpha is never given a value, no p-value is reported, and the CIs are on detector AUC rather than on the logprob difference being compared.

margin_readings.object: Logprob tracking: a permutation two-sample test on the first-token top-k logprobs of one fixed prompt. It compares an LLM API with itself at different times, or an original open-weight model with its fine-tuned, pruned or noised TinyChange variants. The test's detection power is graded by ROC AUC against a null of original/original tests, and the method is then run on 189 real endpoints over 4 months.
margin_readings.reason: The source runs a same-model comparison over time and across modified serving of the same weights (E1), using one fixed prompt (E2) and first-token logprobs (E5). Its verdicts are graded against a null distribution from original/original tests on identical weights (E3). Its permutation test uses only a symbolic, unset significance level; its real-world flags use a 12-SD threshold with no stated level; and its 95% CIs are on detection AUC, not on the compared logprob statistic, so E4 fails. No digest of the item set is published (E6).
margin_readings.hardest_element_why: The paper does define a permutation test whose null is that the two distributions are identical, and it reports 95% CIs. But the significance level is never given a value, and the intervals are on detection AUC rather than on the compared logprob statistic, so it is hard to tell whether the letter of E4 is met.

what_it_does_not_do: It changes no status in the record. The frozen protocol prices C4a from the first reading and its confirmers; this check measures how much that pricing rests on one reader's coding.
